rows.name: VaultPress Backup
rows.reason: WordPress backup/restore service does not provide the requested password-manager clients/extensions. Vendor-operated Jetpack Cloud storage also conflicts with the intermediary-free vault path.

rows.name: Vaultwarden with Bitwarden clients
rows.reason: Vaultwarden containers support Bitwarden Windows/Linux and Chrome/Firefox clients with user-controlled vault/verifier storage. Bitwarden does not guarantee compatibility; local verifier retention and optional outbound integrations were not audited.

rows.name: VaultPress Backup
rows.reason: VaultPress Backup backs up and restores WordPress websites in Jetpack Cloud; it supplies neither a password manager nor the requested desktop and browser vault clients.

rows.name: Psono, fully self-hosted
rows.reason: Psono documents Docker/PostgreSQL and required clients, but authentication hashes need vault-boundary review. Intermediary-free setup remains unverified; current clients do not establish desktop availability by 2023-06-22.

rows.name: Official self-hosted Bitwarden
rows.reason: Official Docker Bitwarden hosts the verifier and encrypted vault with desktop/browser clients. Standard deployment uses outbound connections and installation credentials; absence of all local verifier copies remains unestablished.

rows.name: Dashlane (current web-first product)
rows.reason: Dashlane replaced its Windows desktop app with a web/extension experience, failing the requested desktop-client condition; no user-deployable vault server was verified.

rows.name: KeePassXC with self-managed KDBX synchronization
rows.reason: KeePassXC supplies encrypted KDBX vaults for Windows/Linux and Chrome/Firefox when file synchronization is acceptable. Not a Docker vault server; synchronization, copies and conflicts need separate arrangements.

rows.name: KeeWeb with a user-hosted Docker WebDAV server
rows.reason: KeeWeb with self-hosted Docker WebDAV stores KDBX vaults; serving the app alone provides no vault storage. Use distinct WebDAV credentials; hash persistence, browser compatibility and password-derived client state unverified.

rows.name: Bitwarden, self-hosted
rows.reason: Desktop/browser clients and Docker self-hosting documented. Server stores master-password-derived authentication hash; zero knowledge/self-hosting do not prove strict hash-location requirement. Client persistence and concrete external dependencies unverified.

rows.name: Bitwarden
rows.reason: Its self-hosted Docker server, Windows/Linux desktop clients and Chrome/Firefox extensions fit; offline deployment addresses external service dependencies, and the server stores the authentication verifier.

rows.name: Dashlane (current web-first product)
rows.reason: Current Dashlane lacks required Windows/Linux desktop clients: former desktop apps are unavailable; current families are web, Android, iPhone and macOS. Browser access does not replace separately required desktop versions.

rows.name: Bitwarden
rows.reason: Retain self-hosted Docker Bitwarden for verification with required client categories. Prohibited master-password-hash storage outside the permitted vault and mandatory intermediaries remain unresolved; no decisive forbidden location was established.
